subject: Follow-up: Geo anchoring, backups, and logging controls for Harmonia Health
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Craig Peters <craig.peters@harmoniahealth.com>
Cc: Nina Rao <nina.rao@harmoniahealth.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: Geo anchoring, backups, and logging controls for Harmonia Health

Hi Craig / Nina —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap + our asks so we can scope a short follow-up (technical deep-dive) with your infra/security teams: 

1) Residual requirement recap (from your side):
   - Primary residency: US (data at rest must remain in US regions).
   - Cross-region failover allowed for availability only (EU/APAC failover must be encrypted in transit and at rest; no permanent replication without approval).

2) Key clarifying questions (please confirm):
   - Do patient PII payloads need to be redacted before sending to our hosted Redis KV cache, or is encrypt-at-rest with customer KMS acceptable?
   - Desired maximum recovery point objective (RPO) for model-serving caches and long-term logs? (you mentioned 1 hour in the call — want to confirm)
   - Which logging retention bucket triggers a security review — 90 days or 365 days?

3) What we can offer quickly:
   - Region anchoring/pinning: we can pin production traffic to US-only clusters with automated warm standby in a secondary US region.
   - Cross-region failover: we support automatic failover to a warm standby in another US region; EU/APAC as cold backups only with manual approval and with additional contractual controls.
   - Logging & audit: per-token audit trails available; we can configure log retention window and export to your SIEM via S3/CloudWatch (customer-owned bucket).

Next steps: if you confirm answers to the 3 clarifying questions above, Rishi and I will assemble a one-page scoping note and a timeline for an infra deep-dive (45–60 min). We can also share a short playbook showing failover flow (attached).

Attachments: harmonia_data_map_v1.xlsx (sample mapping you shared), redwood_region_failover_playbook.pdf, SOC2-internal-snapshot-2026-08.pdf

Thanks —
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0172

From: Craig Peters <craig.peters@harmoniahealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Nina Rao <nina.rao@harmoniahealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-30T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Geo anchoring, backups, and logging controls for Harmonia Health

Stephanie — thanks for the clear recap. A few answers inline below.

- PII handling: we prefer encrypt-at-rest with our KMS for long-term storage. For in-flight and cache: short-lived ephemeral encryption is fine but anything persisted beyond 24 hours must be in our KMS-controlled bucket. Can Redwood support customer-managed KMS keys for snapshots/backups?

- RPO: yes, 1 hour target for request-level state. For long-term logs (audit + aggregate telemetry) we’re comfortable with 24 hours, but we need guaranteed export to our S3 within 24 hours.

- Retention trigger: our security bar requires any logs containing PII to be reviewed if retained longer than 90 days. Aggregate non-PII telemetry can be kept 365 days.

We’re happy to schedule the infra deep-dive. Can Rishi/Stephanie propose two slots next week? Nina will lead the technical checklist review.

—Craig
Craig Peters
Head of Platform Ops | Harmonia Health
craig.peters@harmoniahealth.com
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Craig Peters <craig.peters@harmoniahealth.com>, Nina Rao <nina.rao@harmoniahealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Geo anchoring, backups, and logging controls for Harmonia Health

Looping you in — thanks Craig for the clarifications. Quick notes for the internal team so we scope correctly: 

- KMS: Redwood supports customer-managed keys for persistent storage snapshots and S3 exports. Current caveat: KV cache snapshots are supported for customer-managed KMS but will add ~5–10% latency on cold restores; document that in the scoping note.

- RPO/RTO: we can commit to a 1 hour RPO for active request-state (via our continuous KV checkpointing) for US-primary clusters, and 4 hour RPO for cold backups that are copied to cold EU/APAC buckets (requires contract addendum).

- Export/retention: we will provide an automated export to customer S3 within 24 hours (configurable). Retention policy enforcement hooks available via console and API; we should surface the 'PII tag' option so Harmonia can mark specific logs for 90-day review.

Action items for the scoping note (Rishi):
   1) Short summary of limits for customer-managed KMS and expected restore latency.
   2) Flow diagram for automatic US->US warm failover and manual EU/APAC cold restore flow.
   3) Draft contract language options for EU/APAC replication (opt-in only).

Ben/Laura — can you review the draft playbook I’ll attach and flag any SLA/ops caveats? I’ll prep two proposed meeting times once we have a comm window from Harmonia.

Thanks,
Rishi

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Craig Peters <craig.peters@harmoniahealth.com>, Nina Rao <nina.rao@harmoniahealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Geo anchoring, backups, and logging controls for Harmonia Health

Craig / Nina — appreciate the quick reply and helpful constraints. Two proposed slots for the infra deep-dive:

- Tuesday, Oct 5, 10:00–11:00 AM PT
- Wednesday, Oct 6, 2:00–3:00 PM PT

In the deep-dive we’ll cover:
 - KMS key flow and practical restore times (we’ll show numbers from a recent customer benchmark)
 - Failover playbook (automatic US warm failover demo + manual cold restore to APAC/EU)
 - Logging export + retention controls (show how to tag PII and set 90-day review triggers)
 - Contract implications for EU/APAC replication (if you opt in)

I attached an updated copy of the playbook with the warm-standby flow called out (redwood_region_failover_playbook.pdf). Please review if possible before the call.

Next step: confirm which slot works and we’ll send a calendar invite with required pre-reads.

Best,
Stephanie

From: Craig Peters <craig.peters@harmoniahealth.com>

Stephanie — thanks. Wednesday Oct 6, 2:00–3:00 PM PT works for us. Nina and I will review the playbook beforehand.

Couple of last clarifications for the agenda so the right folks join:
 - Please include an ops engineer who can speak to restore SLAs (RTO expectations).
 - Would be helpful to see a short note on log redaction options (client-side vs. server-side) and the tradeoffs.

We’ll send a calendar invite for the internal Harmonia attendees. Looking forward to the session.

—Craig
